findings.title: Error-handler signature breaks process event listeners
findings.description: `index.ts:171-172` registers `handleError` directly as both process listeners. Node supplies an origin string or Promise as the second argument, which now becomes `exitCode`. Both paths reproduce `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` instead of exiting cleanly. Wrap listeners with `(err) => handleError(err)` and add regression tests.

findings.title: Validation ignores the resolved worktree
findings.description: The command discards `worktreeId` and always validates `project.projectPath`. From a registered worktree, explicit local paths are consequently filtered out as outside the document root; without paths, `--fix` modifies the main checkout instead. Resolve the operation path using the existing worktree-aware helper and test both modes.

findings.title: Successful writes are mistaken for successful validation
findings.description: `remaining` contains only original findings whose writes failed or lacked fixes. However, `validateFrontmatter` returns immediately when `docType` is missing. Fixing an inferred `docType` therefore exits successfully even when the newly selected schema exposes missing required fields. Revalidate affected files before determining the exit code, with a regression test for missing `docType`.

findings.title: Date backfill can overwrite the actual modification date
findings.description: For a document with an invalid status and missing `dateUpdated`, validation supplies a date fix copied from `dateCreated`. The status fix stamps today, but the subsequent date fix overwrites it with the old creation date: `updateFrontmatterField` explicitly skips stamping when updating `dateUpdated` itself. Ensure the final date reflects this run’s modification and test combined fixes against real file contents.
